models_evaluated: ML model to non-invasively exclude SBP (20 routine clinical and laboratory variables)

links.outcome: NPV of previously developed SBP model in temporally later national VA cohort
links.effect: Cohort of 4192 patients, 15.0% with SBP; NPV 93.6%, 92.0%, 90.9% at <5%, <10%, <15% thresholds. In 107-patient chart-review subgroup NPV was 100%, 97.5%, 95.4%.
links.quote: At the <5%, <10%, and <15% thresholds for probability of SBP-negativity predicted by the ML model, negative predictive values (NPVs) were 93.6%, 92.0%, and 90.9%, respectively.

screen.reason: The study conducts a retrospective external validation in a contemporary cohort of an existing machine learning model to exclude spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, reporting diagnostic performance metrics without evaluating an implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
